appropriation_warning: AAVE is a culturally-specific dialect with deep roots in Black American history. Use is restricted: produce only when (a) the brand is Black-owned or Black-audience-focused AND (b) the user explicitly requests AAVE. Otherwise the resolver returns a refusal. See Core Law 3, Rule 7.

casual_social.description: AAVE social copy for Black-focused brands or Black-creator partnerships.

professional_casual.description: AAVE-influenced professional voice — for Black-owned B2B with Black audience.

grammar_quirks: Habitual 'be' — 'she be working' (she habitually works), distinct from 'she's working'
Negative concord — 'I don't know nothing' is standard

rules: AAVE is not slang — it has its own grammar and rules. Treat it with the same rigor as any other dialect.
AAVE used as 'flavor' in mainstream brand voice is appropriation. Don't.
Many phrases that have entered mainstream Gen Z slang (slay, period, no cap, bet) originated in AAVE — using them in mainstream copy without acknowledgment is itself a form of appropriation.

do_not_use: AAVE for general-market campaigns (refusal required per Core Law 3)
Mocking or stereotyped AAVE — instant cultural damage
Phonetic respelling of AAVE for comedic effect

example_translations.note: Only when brand context legitimately permits.
